articleTitle: Advanced Machine Learning Techniques for Accurate Diagnosis of Respiratory Diseases Using Vocal Biomarkers
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Respiratory diseases are the leading morbidity in the world. The correct and speedy diagnostic tools are crucially required for efficient management. This paper examines the power of vocal biomarkers in correctly diagnosing respiratory conditions using advanced machine-learning techniques. We have utilized a benchmark dataset and used sophisticated preprocessing techniques to reduce noise and improve the quality of the signals. We extracted diverse numerical features including time domain, statistical, chroma, harmonic, percussive, entropy, peak-based, and rhythm. All these features were compiled structurally in a data frame for further analysis. We adopted a two-step strategy to deal with class imbalance. First, data augmentation techniques such as time stretch, pitch shift, and random crop were applied before feature extraction to increase the sample size; still, class imbalance persisted. Hence, at the later stage of feature extraction, we introduced a hybrid approach that combines random oversampling and undersampling techniques to make classes balanced, thus ensuring accuracy by measuring and adjusting class weights. The performance was evaluated against several classification traditional algorithms and neural networks. All classifiers and neural network architectures returned out-standing results; the ExtraTrees classifier stood out at 99.47%. This paper focuses on the effectiveness of using vocal biomarkers and machine learning models for the non-invasive but accurate diagnosis of respiratory conditions and opens up ways for further smart healthcare solutions.

articleTitle: Secured Text Based CAPTCHA using Customized CNN with Style Transfer and GAN based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)

authors.preferredName: T. M. Amir - UI - Haque Bhuiyan

abstract: A CAPTCHA is one of the popular, secure methods for securing web content from unauthorized access or malicious intruders. It ensures that the user is not a malicious user but a human being. In the early phase of the CAPTCHA scheme, text-based CAPTCHA was widely used, but with recent advancements in deep learning, it has become vulnerable. For this reason, many organizations use image-based CAPTCHA or puzzles to secure their systems. However, these image or puzzle systems sometimes take a lot of time to give access to the system when the user may not understand clearly the images or puzzles. As a result, users sometimes feel bored accessing the systems as it takes a long time. So, considering this scenario, a text-based CAPTCHA has promising demand in terms of usability concerns. The deep learning model can be applied to make complex backgrounds that are hard for machines to understand but easy for human beings; thus, text-based CAPTCHA will be a more secure method compared to images or puzzles. In this paper, we use the style transfer CNN and GAN based deep learning model to make the complex background of the text-based CAPTCHA. Our proposed model can secure a text-based CAPTCHA, and the experimental results show good performance. We try to show the vulnerability of text-based CAPTCHA when we don't use style transfer GAN, and it shows the CAPTCHA recognition rate is near 98.68%. But, with our proposed model, the CAPTCHA recognition rate is 2.1 %, which is a promising result for using text-based CAPTCHA in security systems.

articleTitle: Designing of a PCF Based Ultra-High Negative Dispersion Compensation for Optical Transmission Link
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: This study introduces a dispersion-compensating square photonic crystal fiber (DCS-PCF) aimed at evaluating key properties such as dispersion, dispersion slope, higher- order dispersion, effective mode area, nonlinearity, and the V parameter. The proposed design efficiently compensates for chromatic dispersion, with values ranging from -812.73ps/(nm.km) to -2427.36ps/(nm.km) over the wavelength range of 1340nm to 1640nm. Simulations reveal that the fiber exhibits consid- erable negative dispersion, with a group velocity dispersion (GVD) of -2217.10ps/(nm.km) and a second-order dispersion of 2740.27sp<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> /km at 1550nm. These results indicate that the fiber is a promising option for high-bit-rate transmission systems, providing broadband dispersion compensation and promising potential in nonlinear optical applications.

articleTitle: Assisting the Visually Impaired with Situation Awareness: A New Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Safe and independent mobility presents a significant challenge for visually impaired people, who must detect obstacles and navigate unfamiliar areas. Accurate and efficient solutions for mobility and pathfinding, particularly in recognizing currency, complicated by similar surfaces and sizes, are essential for the visually impaired. This paper proposes a system that assists the visually impaired by recognizing objects and their lateral positions and identifying currency notes. Serving as a comprehensive walking guide for both indoor and outdoor navigation, this system enhances spatial awareness and provides valuable information about surroundings. Our model can recognize fifteen classes of objects and has been evaluated with real-world items. Experimental results demonstrate its superior performance compared to existing approaches, highlighting its effectiveness in improving mobility and independence for visually impaired individuals.

articleTitle: Multi-Class Segmentation of Liver & Tumor Using 2D U-Net with ResNet152 as Backbone
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: One of the main causes of deaths among adults throughout the world is liver cancer. It is difficult and exhaustively time-consuming to identify liver lesion from healthy tissues and cancer tissue from non-cancerous lesion manually in the present scenario of diagnosis which makes medical image segmentation to be very crucial to separate out the liver and corresponding tumor from the CT images of patients' abdomen to diagnose tumor. Numerous studies were done on the topic. With the advancement of technology, autonomous segmentation of liver and tumor has been possible from image datasets of CT or MRI. Though researchers have made significant improvement in this field, there is still scope of enhancing the accuracy of liver and tumor segmentation. The aim of the study is to perform segmentation on liver and tumor classes simultaneously from CT images and enhance the accuracy of segmentation of both liver and tumor. Data augmentation using elastic deformation was performed on the training dataset along with few other augmentation techniques. 2D U-Net model incorporating ResNet152 as the backbone was trained to obtain the segmentation of liver and liver tumor. Dice scores of 96.53% and 81±O.09% are achieved for liver and liver tumor segmentation respectively. The volume overlap error for both liver and tumor are significantly reduced which indicates to a remarkable improvement for the study. The study will help in the clinical practices and decision making in future.

articleTitle: Hybrid Method for Monitoring Sundarbans Mangrove Forest Using Satellite Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: A hybrid method for monitoring Sundarbans mangrove forest using satellite images with machine learning techniques is presented in this paper. The Random Forest algorithm, data scaling, cloud, and shadow masking are used to enhance the precision of land cover classification over the Sundarbans. The study utilizes Landsat 8 imagery to classify land into deep forest, light forest, barren land, and water bodies. Significant fluctuations in land cover types over the analyzed period, with notable variations in forest density, barren land, and water bodies are identified. Normalized Difference Vegetation Index and Normalized Difference Water Index are two popular methods for observing vegetation health and water bodies in remote sensing. But it fails to classify different objects. This paper focuses on solving this issue using machine learning technique by combining the two methods along with the other band's reflectance as a feature to improve the classification and show a great f1 and recall. This study uses a hybrid model to monitor land cover changes in the Sundarbans mangrove forest from 2013 to 2022, achieving an overall accuracy of 0.98. Significant findings include a deep forest cover increase from 52.82% to 55.735%, fluctuations in barren land from 2.04% to a peak of 8.38% in 2021, and a decrease in water bodies from 32.18% to 28.82%, indicating possible changes in river dynamics and hydrological conditions.

articleTitle: Leveraging Attention Mechanisms in Vision Transformer for Human Activity Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Due to the emergence of AI, human activity recognition (HAR) domain is now one of the widely explored challenges expanding its necessity in the field of action data analysis, sports data analysis, fall detection, crime activity recognition, and many more. Yet HAR still experiences many challenges due to environmental dependency, different viewpoints, and illumination conditions making handling inter-class variance and intra-class similarity more challenging. As traditional approaches often rely on the spatial feature extractor for spatial context learning and the temporal feature extractor for training on the temporal domain, without the help of the temporal feature extractor, the spatial feature extractor often fails to generalize the model due to dependency or biases on action environmental aspect. Such a problem arises due to the fact that spatial feature extractors are trained to recognize action by learning to associate a particular background with a specific action using spatial correlation. Although debiasing techniques such as debiasing networks, classifiers, and cascading methods were implemented but could not focus on the specific relation on human or object identifier techniques. In such cases the necessity for implementing an effective spatial feature attention for image data or spatio-temporal attention mechanism for video data are often widely unexplored. The model may concentrate on the most pertinent portions of the input data thanks to attention methods. Based on the limitations of previous work we propose a vision transformer leveraging spatial attention mechanism in image data and spatio-temporal attention in video data-based architecture where we have evaluated the model using real-world datasets UCF Sports Action and BAR dataset getting max accuracy of 96.66% and 64.11% outperforming other state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Enhancing Fire Safety: Encoder-Decoder Based Detection and IoT-Driven Response System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Innovative technologies are crucial for improving fire detection and response systems. An embedded system has been developed to improve fire detection and response by integrating a user mobile application, an admin website, and an IoT-based robot. The mobile application uses the Encoder-Decoder architecture to identify fires from user-captured images, enabling real-time transmission of critical data via the Firebase Realtime Database. The encoder-decoder model performs better with an accuracy of 97.50 %, precision of 97.20 %, recall of 97.10%, and F1-score of 97.05%. The admin website serves as a centralized management platform, utilizing Google Maps API for real-time robot tracking and video streaming from the robot's camera. The system also employs fire and person detection(YOLOv4) algorithms for enhanced monitoring. The robot's construction includes fireproof materials for resilience in fire-prone environments. This comprehensive system offers a robust solution for effective fire detection and response, improving safety and efficiency in emergencies.

articleTitle: Color-Based Auto-Rickshaw Detection Using Convolutional Neural Networks for Intelligent Transportation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: The investigation in this paper is centered on a new methodology for improving the effectiveness of intelligent transportation systems by identifying and distinguishing auto-rickshaws using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). The strategy proposed involves training a CNN model to automatically recognize and differentiate the colors of auto-rickshaws, which in turn significantly enhances the detection capabilities. Using hierarchical convolution feature models, the CNN algorithm independently extracts relevant features from images, thereby aiding in precise object detection. An assessment of the model's performance is conducted using a carefully selected dataset containing 1000 auto-rickshaw images, illustrating a high level of accuracy with minimal margin of error. This research makes a valuable contribution to the advancement of automated transport detection within the realm of traffic management. It presents a more streamlined and impactful methodology aimed at improving the overall efficiency and reliability of the system.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Machine Learning Approach for Electrical Fault Detection and Minimization
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: In the field of electrical power systems, effective fault detection, and minimization are crucial for maintaining system reliability and operational efficiency. This paper introduces machine learning based Adaptive Fault Reduction Algorithm (AFRA), a novel performance optimization approach designed to reduce fault occurrences significantly of electrical power systems. We used a binary classification dataset with a total of 12,001 data samples for this research. Random Forest (RF) model was used for fault detection and compared its performance against the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model. RF model demonstrated accuracy, precision, and recall, with scores of 99.79%, 99.64%, and 99.91 % respectively, compared to the ANN's 99.54%, 99.54%, and 99.45%. By integrating AFRA, we reduced the number of fault events from 5,496 to just 6, achieving a 99.89% reduction. Our approach highlights the importance of optimization in fault detection and minimization methodologies, offering a robust framework for improving system reliability. The promising results achieved by AFRA suggest significant potential for its application in real-time monitoring and dynamic fault detection and minimization in power systems.

articleTitle: Exploring Transformer and Recurrent Neural Models for Sentiment Analysis of Mobile App Reviews
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is one of the important aspects of discovering user opinions and enhancing the quality of products like mobile applications. This study assesses the effectiveness of six prominent Natural Language Processing (NLP) models-BERT, RoBERTa, XLNet, Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU)-in classifying sentiments from a large dataset of Google Play Store reviews. We collected 73,483 reviews from 45 apps, preprocessed the data, and employed two labeling methods: a pre-trained DistilBERT model and K-means clustering. Our results compare transformer-based models, BERT and XLNet, with traditional recurrent models for sentiment analysis of mobile application reviews. The results show that transformer-based models achieve higher accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 scores with DistilBERT pre-trained model labeling. However, no single model strikes a balance between recall and precision using K-means clustering labels. These findings suggest that the choice of labeling method, in addition to the use of advanced transformer models and embeddings, significantly affects model performance.

articleTitle: Enhanced CNN Approaches for Multi-Image Embedding in Image Steganography
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: We unveil a convolutional neural network (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CN N}$</tex>)-architectured steganographic model aimed at concealing multiple secret images in a single cover image, seeking to enhance payload capacity and minimize any encoding or decoding errors. We use a method that employs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CN N}{\mathrm{s}}$</tex> for encoding and decoding, harnessing a multi-scale encoder and a key-based decryption approach for increased security. Steganography is accurately and successfully achieved at two and three image levels by the model. For the use of two-image steganography, an accuracy of 95.16% was achieved for the encoded cover image, and decoding accuracies of 97.16% and 97.28% for secret images 1 and 2, respectively. In the three-image steganography, the accuracy of the coded cover image stood at 93.84%, while the decoded secret images achieved accuracies of 96.39%, 94.82%, and 94.76%. We boosted security by employing cryptographic techniques such as AES and ChaCha20 and instituted key integration at the architectural level. Our findings show the competent encoding and decoding of a range of secret images with enhanced security and noteworthy precision.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Hybrid DRA-SOA for WDM based Fiber Optic Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: In this paper, we present a comprehensive performance analysis of a hybrid Distributed Raman Amplifier (DRA) applied to a wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) based fiber optic transmission system. Analysis is carried out for single mode fiber with hybrid distributed Raman Amplifier (DRA) and semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) based optical fiber transmission system. Results are evaluated in terms of bit error rate (BER), electrical signal to noise ratio (SNR), gain and optical signal to noise ratio (OSNR) for various values of fiber length, pump power and WDM channel number. BER performance is also evaluated for different combinations of hybrid optical amplifier.

articleTitle: Enhancing Heart Disease Diagnosis with Machine Learning Algorithms: An Evaluation on Imbalanced Data and Performance Metrics
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: The precise identification of heart disease is of the greatest significance in enhancing patient outcomes and reducing mortality rates. This research aims to evaluate the effectiveness of machine learning algorithms in the early detection of heart disease. This study employs the dataset of the BRFSS obtained from the Kaggle data archive. The dataset shows a significant imbalance in class distribution. The SMOTE technique was employed to deal with this issue. Hence, the EDA was performed in order to gain a comprehensive understanding of the dataset. Ten algorithms have been employed, utilizing hyper-parameter tuning and 5-fold cross-validation techniques in order to optimize their performance. The evaluation of the machine learning models were performed using five performance metrics. Xgboost appeared as the most effective model during the simulation, achieving an accuracy rate of 92.29%. Yet, both Logistic Regression and Artificial Neural Network shows comparable and satisfactory performance, achieving accuracy of 92.10% and 92.05%, respectively. Therefore, this research has the potential to significantly aid healthcare professionals in effectively treating heart disease, which will encourage the establishment of an efficient e-healthcare system in the near future.

articleTitle: Utilizing Squeeze-and-Excite Mechanisms and Voting Ensembles Technique for Coffee Leaf Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Coffee is a crucial global crop, but its production is often hindered by plant diseases such as coffee leaf rust, coffee berry disease, and bacterial blight, leading to significant yield losses. This study aims to develop an accurate disease detection system for coffee plants using an ensemble of deep learning models. A key contribution of this paper is assessing the impact of adding squeeze-and-excite blocks to Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for enhancing coffee disease detection. We employed several pre-trained CNN models, including MobileNetV2, ResNet152, EfficientNetB7, EfficientNetV2B0, InceptionV3, ResNet50, DenseNet121, and DenseNet201, each modified with squeeze-and-excite blocks to improve feature extraction. The models were trained with three optimizers—Adam, RMSProp, and SGD—with Adam consistently delivering the best results. We then implemented a voting ensemble technique, combining the top-performing CNN models, and found that the ensemble of EfficientNetV2B0 and EfficientNetB7 achieved the highest accuracy of 97.75%. This approach demonstrates the effectiveness of deep learning ensembles and the added benefit of squeeze-and-excite blocks in accurately detecting coffee plant diseases, offering a valuable tool for improving crop management and production.

articleTitle: An Autoencoder-Based Approach of Automatic Writer Identification from Biscriptual Characters
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: In the last decade, automatic writer identification using a convolutional neural network (CNN) has been well studied. For further performance improvement of the writer identification task, a generative adversarial network-based approach is proposed in this paper to find out the corresponding writer of the given handwriting. This is done using an autoencoder model as the generator and a CNN - based classifier model as the discriminator. The autoencoder network generates synthetic images from the input real images which are then fed to the discriminator along with input real images. The synthetic images provide crucial features to the classifier network. Thus, the autoencoder is used as a feature extractor to aid the discriminator for classification. In this work, autoencoder and discriminator models are trained simultaneously on a self-captured dataset containing handwritten characters from two scripts: Bangla and English written by 24 writers three times. Writer identification accuracy of the proposed autoencoder-based approach is 94.24% with a relative improvement of 2.54 % over the accuracy of 91.85% obtained using the same discriminator without the autoencoder. The proposed classifier also outperforms prior models where the accuracy of the second-best model is 90.07%.

articleTitle: ResViT: An Integrated Approach Using ResNet50v2 and Vision Transformer for Enhanced Bangla Handwritten Character Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Bangla, also known as Bengali, serves as the official language of Bangladesh and is the second most widely spoken language in India, flourishing in the voices of 300 million people as a language that bridges hearts and cultures. This linguistic richness is accompanied by a diverse character system and a vibrant literary heritage. However, the transition to digital storage and the conversion of handwritten documents pose notable challenges. ResNet-50 v2, a more advanced version of the ResNet-50 design, was released to improve deep network training by adding identity mappings and residual blocks. The Vision Transformer (ViT) extends the Transformer model from natural language processing to computer vision, employing patch-based image division and self-attention mechanisms for recognizing the global context. This study utilizes a model that combines features from the ViT and ResNet50V2 architectures, incorporating backbones for image processing, global average pooling, feature concatenation, and custom top layers with SoftMax activation, which achieved an impressive 97.21% accuracy on the extensive BanglaLekha- Isolated Dataset containing 166,000 images.

articleTitle: Gesture Controlled Bot with Temperature & Humidity (TH) Sensing Features
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: The paper presents a design and implementation for a gesture-controlled robotic system that can operate in remote regions. This system can send environmental data through wireless data interchange, which a user can then remotely access to operate an application. The robot, being equipped with advanced sensors and communication modules, can capture data about the environment in real-time and perform monitoring and interaction with the environment. What distinguishes it is an intuitive gesture control mechanism that allows a user to interact with and give commands to a robot using natural hand movements, making it easy to use with increased accuracy. This innovative approach allows users to control and navigate the robot using simple palm gestures, fostering an intuitive interaction with the robotic system. The gestures are interpreted by a gyroscope sensor, which directs the robot's movements accordingly. Data collected by this robot is transmitted through a sturdy wireless network to the mobile application, where users can receive, analyze, and respond promptly to this information. It offers a potentially significant benefit for practical applications in harmful working environments, disaster management, or remote exploration where direct human intervention is impossible or hazardous. The paper presents technical specifications, design challenges, and a performance evaluation of the system developed, indicating its usability and robustness in real practical applications.

articleTitle: A Multi-Band Microstrip Patch Antenna for Application in Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Multi-band microstrip patch antennas offer versatility for a wide range of applications. This work presents the design of such an antenna utilizing a slotted rectangular patch on a Rogers RT Duroid 5880 substrate with an inset feed and partially covered ground plane rather than using a fully covered ground. The substrate, Rogers RT Duroid 5880 has a permittivity of 2.2 and a loss tangent of 0.0009. CST STUDIO SUITE has been employed for simulations. The proposed multi-band antenna considerably surpasses its counterpart in terms of performance through multiple frequency bands.

articleTitle: Fetal Head Segmentation and Head Circumference Measurement Using Residual U-Net
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Fetal head segmentation plays an important role in monitoring fetal growth during pregnancy. Automating the segmentation of the fetal head contributes to reducing the workload of healthcare professionals and ensures more consistent and reliable assessments of fetal development. This study introduces a deep-learning-based approach Residual U-Net for fetal head segmentation from ultrasound images and a complete framework for fetal growth monitoring. Residual U-Net utilizes residual connection in its architecture lowering the possibility of vanishing gradients. In the preprocessing stages, contour filling of ground truth, image resizing, image normalization, and data augmentation on an open-source dataset HC18 Grand Challenge was applied. We trained Residual U-Net, U-Net, and Attention U-Net on the same dataset. Evaluation was done on these models based on Dice Coefficient, Jaccard Index, Orientation Angle Difference (OAD), Euclidean Distance (ED), and MSE. The results of the comparative analysis of the models indicated that the Residual U-Net performed better, with an average Dice Coefficient of 97.17% and a Jaccard Index of 94.51%. The performance metrics OAD and ED have average values of 8.29 degrees and 9.58 mm respectively, indicating better Residual U-Net performance than the other models. Also, the calculation of fetal head orientation, and head circumference measurements followed by the calculation of major axis length, minor axis length, and orientation angle was done using ellipse curve fitting.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Based Approach for the Categorization of Actions in Cricket Videos
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Cricket, a widely popular sport, has garnered significant attention, yet the classification of cricket actions remains underexplored in the research domain. This study aims to fill that gap by introducing CricShot13, an extended dataset that includes 3 new action categories-increasing the total to 13 distinct cricket actions-addressing the limitations of existing datasets in terms of scope and real-world applicability. The methodology combines ResNet50 for feature extraction and LSTM for sequence modeling to enhance the accuracy of cricket action classification. Keyframes are extracted from video sequences, and ResNet50 captures spatial features, while LSTM models the temporal relationships between frames. The computational complexity of the ResNet50 + LSTM model, with 512 hidden units, involves 28.90 million parameters, 7.74 Giga FLOPs, and 3.87 Giga MAC operations, indicating its efficiency in handling large-scale datasets. Our proposed approach achieves a classification accuracy of 90.04%. These results underscore the potential of this framework for applications in automated sports video analysis, coaching, and player performance assessment, contributing significantly to the field of computerized sports analysis.

articleTitle: A Collection of Exploratory Data Analysis Techniques for Process Fault Detection in the Tennessee Eastman Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: The Tennessee Eastman process (TEP) is a widely studied industrial benchmark for testing fault detection and diagnosis techniques, given its complexity and the need for reliable fault detection systems in chemical plants. This paper proposes a comprehensive application of exploratory data analysis (EDA) techniques to the TEP dataset to enhance process fault detection and improve understanding of the dataset's features. The proposed methodology involves plotting time series data to capture temporal dynamics and applying Shewhart control charts to monitor process variability. Additionally, deviation atlases are used to detect anomalies across all features, dendrograms are employed to identify hierarchical clusters, and correlation heatmaps visualize interdependencies between process variables. By applying these EDA techniques, patterns and relationships that were less apparent in the raw dataset became identifiable, contributing to a more thorough fault diagnosis. The findings highlight the value of EDA in uncovering hidden insights, which could aid in the development of more robust fault detection algorithms for real-world industrial applications.

articleTitle: Exploring Protein-Protein Interactions Network, Prediction of Drugs and Association of Genes with Diseases Among Anxiety, Insomnia and Depression: A Computational Biology Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: In recent research, computational biology and systems biology have been used to analyze the genetic overlap between anxiety, depression, and insomnia. These psychiatric disorders share significant biochemical and genetic traits, complicating treatment. Using bioinformatics tools like Cytoscape and NetworkAnalyst, genes related to these conditions were collected from the NCBI database, filtered, and analyzed. The study identified 274 genes for anxiety, 620 for depression, and 55 for insomnia, with 21 genes through pre-processing and finding common genes. Afterward, we have to identify the top ten most significant hub genes based on the degree value of genes. In this study, protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks, Protein Drug Interaction(PDI) Networks and Gene Regulatory Networkand. Networks have been investigated, with the aim of originating an important suggestion for designing medications for specific diseases. However, the interactions of proteins with drug molecules help to create an efficient drug design in the future.

articleTitle: Early Diagnosis and Classification of Alzheimer's Disease Using Convolutional Neural Network Based on MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurode-generative disorder that affects memory, thinking, and behavior, gradually leading to mild to severe dementia. Over the past decade, researchers have leveraged deep learning models, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and transfer learning, for the early detection and classification of AD. In this paper, we propose a simple and computationally cost-effective CNN architecture for the early diagnosis and classification of AD. The model was trained using ADNI T1-weighted 2D MRI scans, encompassing cognitively normal (CN) individuals, stable mild cognitive impairment (sMCI) cases, and Alzheimer's dementia (AD) patients. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our model, achieving an accuracy of 98.97%, thereby surpassing most previous studies while utilizing a low-cost custom CNN architecture.

articleTitle: Environmental Sound Pollution Mapping Using Supervised Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: An accurate sound pollution map is necessary in urban environments where sound pollution is prevalent. However, obtaining dense sound pollution data across an area is challenging due to sparse measurements and limited availability of real data. This project aims to develop a framework for predicting dense sound pollution maps based on sparse measurements, leveraging techniques from computer vision. A U-Net Regression model is employed to reconstruct dense sound pollution maps from sparse measurements, portraying the model as a technique for generating sound pollution map images. The performance of the U-Net model is compared with the popular mapping technique called Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), demonstrating that the U-Net model achieves superior accuracy. Furthermore, the ability to generate dense sound pollution maps from sparse data collection via sensors or other methods makes our approach economically and environmentally sustainable.

articleTitle: Optimizing Privacy and Efficiency in Brain Tumor Classification through Advanced Non-IID Federated Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have significantly transformed various fields, especially medical diagnostics. However, centralized deep learning models face significant challenges due to the increasing data volumes from edge devices, including issues related to data privacy and heterogeneity. In this study, a federated deep learning model for brain tumor classification using MRI data is presented. The model enhances the MobileNetV3 architecture with Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) and Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) blocks. A novel non-IID (non-Independent and Identically Distributed) data partitioning strategy, proposed in this study, ensures robust data distribution across clients. Utilizing the Flower framework and the FedOpt algorithm, the model achieved a notable accuracy of 97.40% in eight training rounds, operating efficiently on 15GB of RAM and 10GB of GPU memory. This research underscores the potential of Federated Learning (FL) to address data privacy and resource constraints, demonstrating its efficacy in accurate brain tumor classification. These findings pave the way for future scalable and secure medical AI applications.

articleTitle: An Improved Dependent Task Offloading in Device-Edge-Cloud using Favorite Predecessor Task
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Cloud computing offers fast processing and large storage, while edge computing reduces delay and local device resource issues. A proper offloading strategy is needed among local devices, edge servers, and cloud server to properly utilize the resources. Especially for the dependent task offloading needs extra attention during offloading as result of one task has an impact on other tasks. In device-edge-cloud collaboration, edge selection has a great impact on dependent task offloading. In this paper, we proposed an approach with favorite predecessor (FP) information during edge server selection in a device-edge-cloud environment. This FP-based edge selection strategy reduces the communication delay between the dependent tasks. For this reason, the proposed edge selection approach shows a greater improvement (around 24%) in the overall task completion time than the greedy approach.

articleTitle: LIME-RAY: What Does a Neural Network See from X-Rays?
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: In the field of medical imaging, neural networks have significantly enhanced the analysis and interpretation of X-ray images, providing advanced capabilities in detecting patterns and anomalies. Despite their potential, challenges remain, particularly concerning the interpretability and reliability of these models. The LIME-RAY approach addresses these challenges by integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Long Short- Term Memory (LSTM) networks. This hybrid technique leverages CNNs for spatial feature extraction and LSTMs for temporal pattern recognition, improving the accuracy and interpretability of the model's predictions. Furthermore, Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) are used to provide transparent, interpretable results, crucial for gaining the trust of healthcare professionals. Our approach is validated using a diverse dataset of chest X-rays, including cases of Covid-19, Pneumonia, and Tuberculosis. The proposed method demonstrates superior performance in multi-class disease classification and offers valuable insights into the decision-making process, bridging the gap between complex neural network models and practical healthcare applications.

articleTitle: Analyzing and Forecasting Dew Point Temperature Trends in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Climate change presents substantial worldwide concerns, especially for regions such as Bangladesh, which are exceptionally susceptible due to their geographical and socio-economic circumstances. An important parameter of an environment's weather conditions is the dew point temperature, which significantly influences weather forecasting and climate research. This research intends to expose fundamental trends, seasonal fluctuations, and long-term patterns in the dew point temperature data. The preprocessing steps involved handling missing values, cleaning unnecessary data, and normalizing the dataset to ensure accuracy and consistency. The data was analyzed using correlation analysis, trend analysis, and seasonal decomposition approaches to uncover meaningful insights. In addition, a basic predictive model has been applied to showcase possible forecasting abilities. The results highlight the intricate relationships between dew point temperature and other climatic factors, showcasing both daily and seasonal cycles and long-term trends. The findings of this study are essential information for the development of more accurate and reliable climate models and contribute to a better understanding of climatic changes in Bangladesh.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Smart System for Blind and Visually Impaired People
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: The World Health Organization estimates that 39 million people worldwide are totally blind, out of 284 million with visual impairment. This paper presents a comprehensive methodology and evaluation of a smart system for blind and visually impaired individuals. The system integrates machine learning modules including a Personal Assistant Bot (PAB), Face Recognition, Object Detection using YOLOv7, Optical Character Recognition (OCR), Distance Measurement and Depth Estimation, Navigation, and Bangladeshi Bank Note Detection. The methodology outlines the system's architecture and operational framework, emphasizing real-time processing and user accessibility. Performance evaluations highlight high accuracy rates in Face Recognition (99%), Object Detection (95.7% precision), and Distance Measurement (96.33%). Usability is validated through real-world tests, demonstrating its potential to enhance the autonomy and safety of visually impaired users.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approach for Multi-Label Detection of Abusive Bangla Social Media Comments
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: This paper presents a multilabel classifi-cation model to detect and classify various abuse or bullying content from Bangla social media comments. We utilized an LSTM-based deep learning model to train a classification system using a dataset of 12,557 multilabel comments. The comments were categorized into five categories: Bully, Sexual, Religious, Threat, and Spam. The model achieved an overall accuracy of 93.64% and an AUe of 0.9802. These metrics highlight the model's effectiveness in identifying and classifying abusive content. The results show that the model is robust and dependable, making it a valuable tool for addressing and mitigating various forms of Bangla text-based abuse.

articleTitle: The Keynote Speeches, the Invited Talks, and the Tutorial
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)

articleTitle: A Robust Framework to Secure IoT Sensor Data using Elliptic Curve Cryptography based CP-ABE and Secret Sharing Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: The growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) sector has ushered in an unprecedented era of connectedness, enabling a profusion of applications ranging from smart homes to industrial automation. Researchers predict that by 2030, there will be about 50 billion IoT devices and gadgets globally, completely changing how we interact with our environment. However, because these interconnected systems are vulnerable to many cyber attacks, the rise of IoT devices has also raised worries about data security and privacy. This paper investigates the potential of cryptographic approaches to mitigate IoT data security issues. It proposes an all-encompassing framework to protect IoT data from various threats and vulnerabilities. The framework leverages the robustness of the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) as the primary data encryption technology. Additionally, it integrates ciphertext-policy attribute-based encryption (CP-ABE) in conjunction with Elliptic Curve Cryptography to enable fine-grained access control, ensuring that only authorized entities can access specific IoT data. Furthermore, to fortify the encryption process, the framework implements a secret sharing method for the encryption key, distributing the key across multiple entities, reducing the risk of a single point of failure. The suggested framework seeks to improve the security posture of IoT systems by integrating these cryptographic algorithms and guaranteeing the confidentiality, integrity, and accessibility of data in IoT contexts.

articleTitle: Advancing Monkeypox Diagnosis: A Novel Approach Using a Custom Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: A few red bumps that might seem innocent at first may hold a darker secret-monkeypox, a viral disease that is a member of the chicken pox family. The issue arises since monkeypox is highly contagious and therefore any close contact with the victim can be detrimental. Often the person can get assured after a series of diagnostic tests and examinations such as PCR and viral culture to confirm the presence of Monkeypox but they involve invasive and painful sample collection procedures, like blood draws which could be painful. Moreover, the process involves multiple tedious steps which can devour a lot of valuable time and are relatively expensive, making it less accessible to all the people. This research aims to make the diagnostic process efficient, cost-effective, and accessible, ultimately improving the identification and management of Monkeypox cases in resource-constrained environments. To improve monkeypox diagnosis, this study utilized a dataset of whole-body skin images captured by a smartphone and developed a novel custom neural network consisting of 41 layers where separable convolutional layers techniques as well as fire module were used alongside the traditional convolution layers. Our proposed model outperformed other state-of-the-art methods with an accuracy of 96.88%, a precision of 95.30%, a recall of 99.24%, and an Fl-score of 97.23%, the classification model shows how accurately it can identify monkeypox cases with the help of computer-assisted techniques using smartphone.

articleTitle: Wi-Fi CSI-based Vibration Sensing for Industrial Fault Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: In the modern landscape of ubiquitous wireless technologies, WiFi sensing has emerged as a promising method to gather environmental data through WiFi Channel State Information (CSI). This paper presents a comprehensive framework designed to identify frequency levels of vibrating objects and detect faults in industrial settings. Passive sensing using CSI data as in the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), wireless sensing has become increasingly popular for fault detection. The proposed methodology comprises four key stages: setting up the experimental environment, collecting CSI data, preprocessing the data, and predicting frequency levels and faults. CSI data were meticulously gathered across a frequency range of 0 to 20 Hz. Subsequent data processing involved feature selection using Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross-Validation (RFECV) and comparison with other feature selection techniques after preprocessing the raw CSI data. The processed data were then analyzed using both Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) models. Among the ML models, CatBoost demonstrated superior performance for frequency identification, achieving an accuracy of 95.52%. For fault detection, the Random Forest (RF) model excelled, attaining an accuracy of 98.77%. These models were evaluated based on various metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and f1 score, confirming their efficacy and robustness in industrial applications. The findings highlight the potential of Wi-Fi CSI-based sensing as a reliable and efficient solution for industrial fault detection and frequency identification.

articleTitle: Integrated Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Analysis Reveals Shared Key Candidate Biomarkers and Therapeutic Targets in Ulcerative Colitis and Colorectal Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: The interplay between ulcerative colitis (UC) and colorectal cancer (CRC) has garnered significant research interest due to their potential shared molecular mechanisms. This study aims to identify common significant biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets for UC and CRC. We utilized two microarray datasets to perform differential expression analysis, identifying DEGs for both conditions. Subsequent ML-based gene selection was conducted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) algorithm models on the respective datasets. Common ML-based DEGs were then identified and a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed using the STRING database. The PPI network was visualized and analyzed in Cytoscape, with the top ten hub genes identified using the Degree method in the cytoHubba plugin. The hub genes identified were CDC20, ANLN, HMMR, CCNB1, CDK1, KIF20A, ECT2, KIF11, NUF2, and CCNA2. These genes were further validated through survival analysis, establishing their significance in patient outcomes. Finally, we explored the drug-gene interaction network to identify potential therapeutic drugs targeting these hub genes. This comprehensive bioinformatics approach provides insights into the shared molecular pathways in UC and CRC and highlights potential therapeutic targets for future research and drug development.

articleTitle: English Offensive Text Detection Using CNN Based Bi-GRU Model
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Over the years, the number of users of social media has increased drastically. People frequently share their thoughts through social platforms, and this leads to an increase in hate content. In this virtual community, individuals share their views, express their feelings, and post photos, videos, blogs, and more. Social networking sites like Facebook and Twitter provide platforms to share vast amounts of content with a single click. However, these platforms do not impose restrictions on the uploaded content, which may include abusive language and explicit images unsuitable for social media. To resolve this issue, a new idea must be implemented to divide the inappropriate content. Numerous studies have been done to automate the process. In this paper, we propose a new Bi-GRU-CNN model to classify whether the text is offensive or not. The combination of the Bi-GRU and CNN models outperforms the existing models.

articleTitle: Dynamic Authentication Scheme for Advanced Security in Federated Metaverse Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: The Metaverse is an open world constantly evolving as people provide new forms of interaction in the digital space with the help of technologies such as blockchain, augmented reality, virtual reality, and artificial intelligence. An evolution of this concept is the Federated Metaverse, it considers the digital world as a network of Metaworlds all managed independently. Specifically, identity verification represents a key component of this federated architecture in order to manage permissions and authentication relative to each Metaworld's regulations. With such diversification of use cases in the Metaverse, the aspect of security is critical as the Metaverse becomes part of people's regular lives. Based on the needs regarding algorithms and based on multiple factors for the improved security, this paper has developed a dynamic authentication scheme for the Federated Metaverse. This scheme enables dynamic authentication through a handshake process that efficiently gathers security requirements, allowing for scalable solutions that adapt to either simple or advanced security measures, thus balancing security, privacy, and usability with authentication speed based on the specified requirements.

articleTitle: V-Shopper: A Virtual Automatic Shopping System Based on 5 DOF Robotic Arm with Real-Time Visualization and Billing
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: In an era where e-commerce demands are soaring, the quest for an immersive and efficient shopping experience is more relevant than ever. This paper introduces a cutting-edge virtual reality based automatic online shopping system that offers real-life shopping experience in a virtual platform via real-time product visualization and robot-based automated product collection. Central to our system is a low-cost, 5-degree-of-freedom (DOF) robotic arm mounted on a line-following robot, equipped with basic Wi-Fi connection and an online user-friendly shopping platform. Customers can browse a fully designed e-commerce website where products are listed and view a live video feed via an ESP32 camera, allowing them to virtually inspect and select products with precision. Unlike current solutions, our platform incorporates a robust closed loop feedback system utilizing force-measuring sensors to ensure secure and precise material gripping, proper weight lifting, and handling of products, addressing issues related to varying weights, shapes, and sizes. The system's open-source software, requiring no paid licenses, enhances its accessibility and cost-effectiveness. Rigorous testing across diverse environments and product types demonstrated the system's ability to deliver accurate, reliable performance, even under challenging conditions. By bridging the gap between digital and physical shopping experiences, our solution not only streamlines the process but also elevates it with superior virtual reality integration, add secured communication, and seamless billing satisfaction, low cost operation, setting a new benchmark in the realm of online retail.

articleTitle: Brain Stroke Prediction using Explainable Machine Learning and Time Series Feature Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: A brain stroke happens when blood flow to a part of the brain is interrupted or reduced. It is a critical medical condition that demands timely detection to prevent severe outcomes, including permanent paralysis and death. This research focuses on predicting brain stroke using machine learning (ML) and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). We employ a comprehensive dataset featuring various parameters associated with brain stroke such as age, Body Mass Index (BMI), average glucose, smoking, etc. and related diseases like hypertension and heart disease. Our objective is to develop an automated system that can accurately predict the possibility of a brain stroke. To achieve this, we utilized several classification ML models, including Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT), Adaptive Boosting (AdaB), and Categorical Boosting (CatB). Additionally, we incorporated time series feature engineering (TSFE) techniques, such as Lag Features (LF) and Rolling Statistics (RS), to enhance prediction accuracy. Our research introduces a cross-validation (CV) approach, highlighting that the XGB model with Rolling Statistics (XGB-RS) stands out as the top performer. This model achieved impressive results, with average metrics of 98.06% accuracy, 90.57% precision, 88.46% recall, 99.12% specificity, and an F1 score of 89.4%. Additionally, it utilizes a Confusion Matrix (CM) and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Curve. To interpret these outcomes, we employ Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), underscoring the importance of understanding the contributing factors. This research provides valuable insights into improving long-term health conditions, reducing mortality rates, and supporting healthcare professionals in managing brain stroke.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Text Summarization Efficiency of Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Text summarization is crucial in condensing lengthy texts into concise summaries, enabling efficient information retrieval and content evaluation. Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as pivotal tools in this domain, demonstrating a remarkable ability to generate coherent summaries across diverse languages and domains. This study explores the effectiveness of LLMs, particularly Llama-2 and Gemma, in text summarization tasks. The study evaluates how well these LLMs autonomously generate summaries using zero-shot prompt engineering and supervised fine-tuning. Evaluation metrics such as BLEU, ROUGE, and BERTScore are utilized to evaluate the quality and coherence of the generated summaries. The study shows notable differences between Llama-2 and Gemma, with Llama-2 outperforming particularly well after fine-tuning. It achieves higher scores across all evaluation metrics, highlighting its ability to generate contextually relevant summaries more effectively than Gemma. Efforts to optimize Large Language Models (LLMs) for summarization should prioritize refining model architectures, exploring innovative fine-tuning methods, and expanding training datasets. These efforts are essential to fully harness the potential of LLMs in producing high-quality summaries across diverse domains and linguistic contexts.

articleTitle: Regional Heatwave Prediction Using Deep Learning Models In Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: With the growing threat of heatwaves in Bangladesh due to climate change, predicting heatwave days has become vital for effective mitigation measures. In this study, a robust dataset of 25 years, acquired through the Bangladesh Meteorological Department, is capitalized to explore Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM), Bi-directional LSTM (Bi-LSTM), and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models for predicting heatwave in four heatwave-prone districts of Bangladesh: Dhaka, Rajshahi, Bogra and Dinajpur. The selected features are maximum temperature, humidity, dew point temperature, pressure, wind speed and sunshine. The dataset was divided into 80% for training, 10% for validation and 10% for testing. The predictive performance of Bi- LSTM, Conv1D, and LSTM models was evaluated with Accuracy, Fl-score, R2 score. Bi-LSTM consistently showed high accuracy, with Dhaka and Rajshahi achieving 96.96% and 97.40%, respec-tively, and Bogra recorded the highest accuracy at 99.57%. In Dhaka, Bi-LSTM had the highest accuracy at 96.96%, followed by Conv1D at 95.65%, and LSTM at 93.04%. For the F1-score, Bi-LSTM led with 86.27%, and in R2 score, it performed best with 77.40%. These results demonstrate the superior performance of the Bi-LSTM model in predicting heatwave days, making it a beneficial tool for early warning and preparedness efforts. Despite the predominant use of statistical models on Bangladeshi datasets, this study explores the novel application of deep learning models like Bi-LSTM and CNNs for heatwave classification, which offer better identification of complex spatiotemporal patterns and are more resistant to anomalies.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Capability of Single Error Correction and Double Error Detection Method
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach to tolerate double-bit soft errors. Soft error is becoming a matter of concern for computer systems. Critical systems and systems operated in electronic hostile environments are at high risk due to the sudden occurrence of soft errors. This paper proposes a new method for correcting double-bit soft errors in an n-bit dataword where n can be any integer number. The most efficient part of this paper is the temperate use of redundant bits. In this paper, the XOR method is used along with the SECDED (Single Error Correction - Double Error Detection) code to enhance the capability of SECDED toward double-bit error correction. This paper corrects all two-bit errors and can also correct almost every type of triple-bit error.

articleTitle: Streamlining Global Visa Processing and Document Verification: A Self-Sovereign Identity System for Secure and Efficient Visa Processing Using Hyperledger Indy
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Travel and tourism have become vital economic sectors, significantly contributing to global GDP and employment. In the era of global travel, the fastest visa processing and comprehensive immigration document verification are indispensable for both security and convenience. Traditional procedures had inefficiencies, long processing delays, and limited cross-border cooperation between countries and immigration agencies. However, rising crime rates pose substantial challenges, especially when offenders exploit international travel to evade justice. This paper proposes a Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI) based system leveraging Hyperledger Indy to revolutionize visa processing and verification, addressing concerns of travel history and potential criminal activity. The system utilizes Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) and Verifiable Credentials (VCs) to enable secure, decentralized communication among key entities: passport offices, visa centers, and immigration authorities. The interoperability between different countries' networks is facilitated by Hyperledger Cacti, ensuring seamless collaboration across borders. This allows for efficient data exchange, significantly reducing the time needed for application processing while enhancing security. Through this innovative approach, the system enhances the integrity of travel records, expedites visa applications, ensures compliance with data privacy regulations, and strengthens border security, ultimately protecting national interests.

articleTitle: DeepResVit: A Hybrid Deep Learning Approach for Ovarian Cancer Classification with XAI
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Ovarian cancer is one of the most prevalent cancers in women and primarily results from the uncontrollable growth and division of abnormal cells in the ovary. Early detection is essential for improving survival rates, yet traditional diag-nostic techniques struggle to detect the disease at an early stage. This study aims to address this challenge by proposing a robust hybrid deep learning model named DeepResVit, which integrates both the pre-trained ResNet-152 and Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures for ovarian cancer classification. Several preprocessing techniques, such as data augmentation, image resizing, random horizontal flip, and random vertical flip were applied to improve the image quality. The model is further enhanced with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques, such as Grad-CAM++, to improve the transparency and interpretability of predictions. In experimental evaluations, DeepResVit achieved outstanding performance with a test accuracy of 98.65%, precision of 98.65%, recall of 98.68%, and F1-score of 98.65%. Custom-connected layers, data augmentation, and L1 regularization strengthened the model's robustness across diverse histopathological images. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of DeepResVit in accurately detecting ovarian cancer at an early stage while providing clear insights into the model's decision-making process.

articleTitle: Exploring the Efficacy of Modified Transfer Learning in Identifying Parkinson's Disease Through Drawn Image Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurode-generative condition characterized by the death of dopaminergic neurons, leading to various movement disorder symptoms. Early diagnosis of PD is crucial to prevent adverse effects, yet traditional diagnostic methods are often cumbersome and costly. In this study, a machine learning-based approach is proposed using hand-drawn spiral and wave images as potential biomarkers for PD detection. Our methodology leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs), transfer learning, and attention mechanisms to improve model performance and resilience against overfitting. To enhance the diversity and richness of both spiral and wave categories, the training dataset undergoes augmentation to increase the number of images. The proposed architecture comprises three phases: utilizing pre-trained CNNs, incorporating custom convolutional layers, and ensemble voting. Employing hard voting further enhances performance by aggregating predictions from multiple models. Experimental results show promising accuracy rates. For spiral images, weighted average precision, recall, and F1-score are 90%, and for wave images, they are 96.67%. After combining the predictions through ensemble hard voting, the overall accuracy is 93.3%. These findings underscore the potential of machine learning in early PD diagnosis, offering a non-invasive and cost-effective solution to improve patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation in Satellite Imagery: An Attentive U - Net Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Semantic segmentation is a computer vision technique that assigns a distinct class label to every pixel in an image, generating a segmentation map where each pixel belongs to a specific category. This enables various applications, such as automatic and in-depth land cover and land use analysis, tracking urbanization, deforestation, road, and building detection, disaster response, traffic management, city planning, and environmental monitoring. Encoder-decoder-based architectures excel in semantic segmentation tasks than traditional CNN-based methods because they can extract hierarchical features, combine contextual and spatial information, and accurately reconstruct segmentation maps. In this paper, Attention U-Net, where the attention mechanism is introduced to the modified version of U-Net, is implemented for semantic segmentation in satellite images. Instead of just focusing on extracting features, the proposed method emphasizes making accurate segmentation output. The segmentation quality of each model was assessed using performance metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and IoU score. The findings suggest that the Attention U - Net model surpasses other variations, attaining a higher IoU score of 0.7959 and exhibiting strong segmentation abilities across several land cover categories, such as water bodies, land, roads, buildings, and vegetation. Furthermore, by visual analysis of the results, it becomes apparent that the Attention U-Net is remarkably proficient at accurately capturing intricate details in satellite imagery,

articleTitle: IoT-based Smart Water Consumption Monitoring System for Residential Complex
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Freshwater scarcity is a pressing global matter right now and the importance of putting more focus on monitoring and conserving water resources is growing. This research presents the development of a cost-effective, scalable, easy to maintain IoT-based water consumption monitoring system for residential buildings using Long Range Communication technology (LoRa). The key components of the system include IoT-enabled smart water meters installed in each residential unit with LoRa communication modules for long-range, low-power communication which enables data transmission over considerable distances with minimal energy consumption, and an open-source IoT analytics platform called ThingSpeak. The water sensors capture real-time data on water usage, which is then transmitted to ThingSpeak through a microcontroller and WiFi module using LoRa communication. Sample tests demonstrate the system's effectiveness in measuring water usage and flow rate at a given time, offering real-time visualization and user engagement, making it an essential tool for promoting sustainable water management practices.

articleTitle: Enhancing Transparency in DDoS Detection on SDN Using Explainable ML Models
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Software-Defined Networking (SDN) is a networking approach that allows network administrators to define and manage network behavior through software rather than relying on physical hardware configurations. SDN can be both beneficial and challenging. The benefits include centralized management, automated detection, and efficient mitigation. SDN's programma-bility enables rapid deployment of DDoS defenses and real-time analytics. However, SDN's complexity and dependency on software can make it vulnerable to DDoS attacks. Additionally, SDN's centralized architecture can create a single point of failure, making it crucial to design robust networks and implement proactive security measures. In this research, we aim to address the DDoS attack detection using machine learning-based meth-ods. Our research is conducted on the CIC-DDoS2019 dataset and the result demonstrates that our optimized XGBoost model with chosen hyperparameters surpasses existing models with significant improvements in attack detection, achieving a recall score of 100%. Explainable AI (XAI) techniques were applied to provide insights into the model's decision-making process.

articleTitle: Integrating Feature Selection and Extraction with Tuned Multilayer Perceptrons for Predicting Student Dropout Risk in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Every year, thousands of students drop out of educational institutions, significantly undermining the effectiveness of our education systems. Identifying factors contributing to dropout and implementing early interventions based on these factors is crucial. However, the acquisition of institutional data poses significant challenges due to privacy and security concerns. Moreover, while the availability of educational datasets is increasing, these often suffer from poor structure or organisation or lack relevance to specific problems. Additionally, the tools commonly used in pedagogy may lack optimised processes. In this paper, we have proposed a novel approach to predict dropout-related factors based on socio-economic and academic features. Our method combines Random Forest for feature selection and Principal Component Analysis for feature extraction, followed by training a finely tuned neural network to classify potential dropouts effectively. We have evaluated our model on two benchmark datasets SATDAP and ICFES, achieving accuracies of 90.08% and 80.03%, respectively, thereby outperforming state-of - the-art machine learning classifiers. This demonstrates the potential of our approach in addressing the dropout challenge in educational settings.

articleTitle: Secure and Transparent Driver Profiling Using Blockchain and IPFS for Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: The existing driver reputation management system, constrained by outdated regulations, suffers from issues like fraudulent manipulation of driver points, obscured driver histories, slow performance, and data leakage vulnerabilities compromising public road safety and personal data integrity. This paper introduces a blockchain-based driver reputation management system integrating the Interplanetary File System (IPFS), machine learning, a dynamic reputation calculation algorithm, and cryptographic encryption. The implementation results in enhanced accuracy in tracking driver performances, improved public and road safety, and more reliable driver assessments. This innovative approach not only addresses inefficiencies in traditional systems but also offers a scalable, secure solution for transportation management in smart cities, providing a nuanced, real-time evaluation of driver behaviour.

articleTitle: A Compact Wideband Patch Antenna for Ka-Band and 5G mm-Wavelength Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: In the current era, 5G technology is crucial for fast and secure data communication. A wide bandwidth allows high data rates and the ability to simultaneously manage large amounts of information. The recommended antenna enables a wide bandwidth of 9.94 GHz, covering frequencies from 27.92 GHz to 37.86 GHz, ideal for Ka-band and 5G applications. This compact antenna, with dimensions of 7×8×0.8 mm3, employs Rogers R04350 (lossy) material as the substrate, featuring a dielectric constant (∊r) of 3.66 and a loss tangent (δ) of 0.0037. It achieves a peak gain of 7 dBi and a directivity of 7.99 dBi at 37.86 G Hz, along with a radiation efficiency of 80 %. The antenna also demonstrates a minimum return loss of −27.76 dB at 35.92 GHz and maintains VSWR within the acceptable range across the entire frequency band. These outcomes affirm that the antenna is highly suitable for 5G mobile communication and various Ka-band applications.

articleTitle: YOLO Goes Green: Unveiling Sundarbans Biodiversity using Leaf Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: In the Sundarbans mangrove forest, the identification of plant species is crucial for ecological research, tourism, and conservation efforts. This study presents an innovative image-based plant recognition model for the Sundarbans, leveraging deep convolutional neural networks (DCNN). A comprehensive dataset of 28,081 high-resolution images, representing 36 different plant species native to the Sundarbans, was compiled to facilitate the model's development. Moreover, transfer learning was applied to a pre-trained YOLOv8 model, enabling the system to use previously learned features while adapting to the unique characteristics of Sundarbans flora. The results demonstrate that transfer learning is highly effective in identifying Sundarbans plant species. In addition, the high performance of the model has been further explained through the incorporation of the Grad-CAM technique. This approach allows researchers and conservationists to visually understand which parts of an image contribute the most to the prediction of the model, thus fostering greater trust and insight into the decision-making process of the neural network. Furthermore, six different YOLO pre-trained models were compared, with the YOLOv8x-cls model outperforming the other variants. In particular, the YOLOv8x-cls model achieved a top-1 accuracy of 98.38% and a top-5 accuracy of 99.76%.

articleTitle: Classification of Ovarian Cancer by Machine Learning Models and its Analysis by Explainable Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Ovarian cancer is a cancerous tumor in the ovary. To assist with its diagnosis, machine learning models can be used to predict ovarian cancer based on the data available from medical tests. We use data (in terms of features for a number of patients) from Kaggle and according to the mutual information scores of the features, human epididymis protein 4 and carbohydrate antigen 125 appear to be the most important features in the dataset. We came up with a framework that employs a variety of machine learning models and a neural network to predict whether a patient has ovarian cancer or not. Most of the machine learning models are fairly good for prediction, however, our findings indicate that Random Forest, with accuracy of 85.4 %, is the best possible classifier; it exhibits a recall of 85 % to demonstrate its effectiveness in having less false negatives. Neural network like Multi-layer Perceptron also has the ability to perform almost as good as Random Forest if we use a dataset containing some of the best features. Further, we explain the prediction of a test instance by means of an explainable artificial intelligence tool called Local Interpretable Model Agnostic Explanations (LIME).

articleTitle: Statistical Similarity Measure for Interpreting Important Features in Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Machine learning(ML)-based feature selection algorithms use specific techniques to assess feature relevance. In medical datasets, many attributes can be irrelevant for classification. Many features in these datasets are often irrelevant for classification tasks, and removing them can improve efficiency without sacrificing accuracy. The study uses techniques like Random Forest and Permutation Feature Importance to determine significant features from datasets provided by the University of California, Irvine (UCI). To assess feature relevance, statistical tests such as the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic and t-test are employed, along with the Mahalanobis Distance Measure to filter important features. The research highlights the value of feature selection in improving model performance. The dataset used demonstrated a 96% accuracy, 97% F1 score, and 98% AUC in 5-fold cross-validation with full features. When reduced to 50% of the most relevant features, the performance improved with an AUC of 99%, indicating better results with fewer features. The findings suggest that statistical similarity metrics like the Mahalanobis Distance Measure can be effective for feature selection, improving model efficiency and accuracy.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of a Double-Sided MIC Technology-Inspired Microstrip Array Antenna Using FSS Reflector
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: This study investigates incorporating a 7 x 7 frequency selective surface (FSS) reflector array with a double- sided MIC technology-inspired 2x2 microstrip array antenna to enhance performance at a frequency of 10 GHz. Conventional microstrip antennas encounter constraints in enhancing gain without structural alterations. Significantly gain enhancement is achieved by placing the FSS reflector 17 mm (equivalent to beneath the antenna. The combined system achieves a reflection coefficient of less than −30 dB and a gain of 15 dBi, in contrast to 11.9 dBi without the reflector.
