This demonstrates enhanced directional transmission and signal strength. Because of these improvements, the proposed arrangement is well-suited for telecommunications, RADAR, satellite, and UAV applications. The significant improvements resulting from this integration have been confirmed through extensive simulations.

articleTitle: Enhancing Marine Radar Security Through Semi-Supervised Learning: A Self-Training Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Marine radar systems are essential for maritime safety but are increasingly vulnerable to cyber-attacks. This research presents a method to improve marine radar security using semi-supervised learning with a Self-Training Classifier. By leveraging both labeled and unlabeled data, this approach enhances the detection of cyber threats. The RadarPWN dataset, consisting of network traffic from marine radar systems, was preprocessed and used to train a RandomForestClassifier (RFC). Through iterative training, high-confidence predictions from unlabeled data were incorporated to improve detection accuracy. The method achieved 99.99% accuracy, effectively identifying multiple attack types, including scaling, addition, rotation, move, translation, removal, and Denial of Service (DoS) attacks. This approach strengthens the resilience of marine radar systems, addressing the challenge of limited labeled data in maritime cybersecurity.

articleTitle: Early-Stage Diabetes Risk Prediction Utilizing Machine Learning with Explainable AI from Polynomial and Binning Feature Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Diabetes is a chronic disease that affects a significant portion of the global population. It occurs when the body cannot produce enough insulin or effectively use the insulin it produces, leading to elevated blood glucose levels. Diabetes is a major contributor to various severe health conditions, including heart disease, stroke, kidney failure, and nerve damage. Early detection of diabetes is crucial in mitigating these associated health risks and improving patient outcomes. In response to the increasing prevalence of diabetes, we have developed an automated system for Early-Stage Diabetes Risk Prediction (ESDRP). This study utilizes a dataset consisting of 16 features from 520 instances. We applied multiple Machine Learning (ML) models, including XGBoost (XGB), Bootstrap Aggregating (BAG), Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost), Light Gradient Boosted Machine (LGBM), and Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT), both with and without feature generation techniques. Specifically, we explored polynomial and binning feature generation methods. Our findings indicate that the polynomial feature generation technique combined with XGB yielded the highest performance, achieving an accuracy of 99.22%, precision of 100%, recall of 98.15%, specificity of 99.06%, and F1-score of 100%. Additionally, all the ML models were evaluated using confusion matrices (CM) and ROC curves, with the average performance across 10-fold cross-validation demonstrating robust predictive capabilities. Furthermore, to establish trust in our model's predictions, we incorporated two explainable AI (XAI) methods: LIME and SHAP. These techniques helped us understand feature importance, the decision-making process of the models, and enhanced the reliability of our results. Our automated system aims to assist individuals of all ages and healthcare systems in identifying ESDRP, thereby supporting informed decision-making and improving global health outcomes.

articleTitle: A Bioinformatics Approach to Identify Hub Genes Across Schizophrenia, Anxiety, Bipolar Disorder, and Depressive Disorder for Network-Based Drug Discovery
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Mental health disorders represent a significant challenge in society, requiring immediate attention and comprehensive knowledge to mitigate their widespread impacts. Although considerable research has focused on hub gene identification for one or two illnesses, there is a lack of literature examining multiple common disorders and their implications for drug discovery. This study utilizes a bioinformatics methodology to identify shared and critical genes linked to anxiety disorders, bipolar disorders, schizophrenia, and depressive disorders, along with potential therapeutic targets for these conditions. We methodically collected gene-related data from the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) for these disorders. Through protein-protein interaction analysis, we discovered hub genes, including GSK3B, MAPT, NR3C1, ESR1, TNF, SOD1, APP, CREB1, NOS1, APOE, GNB3, DISC1, SIRT1, CACNA1C, and BDNF. Additionally, we identified potential therapeutic agents targeting these hub genes, including Kaempferol, Sim-vastatin (CTD 00007319), Luteolin, Clozapine (CTD 00005693), Curcumin, Resveratrol, Melatonin (CTD 00006260), Felodipine, Apigenin, Docosahexaenoic Acid, Diazepam, and Alprazolam, using the DSigDB database. This study seeks to elucidate the genetic connections across mental health diseases and to find therapeutic compounds that may provide common treatment advantages.

articleTitle: Biologically Inspired Network Design to Train Only Through Forward Pass
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Commonly used neural network architectures in the industry almost entirely rely on backpropagation techniques like SGD to minimize the error of the network. It is not only computationally expensive but needs to be done in a separate phase before inference time. To address these issues, this paper introduces a perceptron architecture that can train neural networks without backpropagation, a design inspired by the recent discovery of Brain Criticality Theory in neuroscience and the Hebbian Learning process of the biological brain. These neural computation units, called “Biceptrons” use a binary system to indicate either an active or inactive state in the network, analogous to the spike potentials of cortical neurons. The weights are adjusted with a special training algorithm only through a forward pass during inference time, where the weights gradually reach a steady state while learning the feature representation of the dataset. The authors present some toy problems of neural networks built using these “Biceptrons” units to demonstrate the application of this architecture.

articleTitle: Modeling of 5G-Enabled Hybrid Visible Light Communication Systems for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Vehicle-to-vehicle Visible Light Communication (V2V-VLC) is a promising technology in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) that utilizes visible light signals for communication between autonomous vehicles (AVs). In this paper, we present a new 5G-enabled hybrid V2V-VLC model for AVs complying with IEEE 802.15.7 standard. The proposed hybrid model incorporates both Line-of-Sight (LoS) and Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) modules that have low complexity and high reliability. We evaluate the efficacy of the proposed hybrid model by transmitting 100 Mb, 200 Mb, and 300 Mb of data for both LoS and NLoS modules. We further evaluate the reliability of the proposed model by implementing it under different weather conditions and transmission distances. It is found that our proposed hybrid V2V-VLC model offers an effective way to communicate between AVs by its backlight (red LED), especially in accurately identifying braking events of the preceding vehicle for different longitudinal distances, lighting, and weather conditions. Therefore, our proposed model can improve road safety and overall communication efficiency.

articleTitle: Prediction of Movie Box Office Success Using YouTube Trailer Comments and Wikipedia Data
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: The prediction of a movie's success or failure at the box office is a challenging task due to the various factors that influence it. In addition to the audience's reception to a movie's trailer, key factors such as - the popularity of actors and actresses starring in the film, the movie studio's marketing efforts, and critical reception playa significant role in determining a movie's box office performance. Social media also has a prominent influence over box office performance with more and more people using social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, and YouTube to express their opinions and feelings on movies. This research aims to predict the box office success of movies using machine learning algorithms by combining contemporary Wikipedia data with the opinions expressed by audiences through comments on YouTube movie trailers.

articleTitle: Unveiling Fake News with an Attention-Based CNN Model Using Hybrid Features
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT)
abstract: Sophisticated detection mechanisms are required to protect the integrity of information in the digital age, as the widespread dissemination of false news on social media platforms has become a critical challenge. To tackle the practical issue of spreading false information, there is an urgent need for reliable systems that can effectively identify and counteract the propagation of fake news. This work presents a novel method for identifying fake news by combining sophisticated encoding techniques and utilizing deep learning architectures. Our approach integrates TF-IDF, CountVectorizer (CV), and Word2Vec (W2V) techniques for encoding. These techniques are coupled sequentially to capture the subtle details in fake news content successfully. Through the utilization of attention-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models, we improve the comprehension and categorization of intricate textual material. Our methodology prioritizes scalability to efficiently analyze big datasets while retaining high detection accuracy in many situations and languages. Our approach has been thoroughly tested and proven to be strong and applicable in a wide range of false news situations. We have attained a state-of-the-art level of precision, with an accuracy of 99.11 %, by employing an attention-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) coupled CountVectorizer and Word2Vec embeddings,
